title: the proof standard's classes
line: a household's census and a birth register read by data/evidence-classes.csv: the census a derivative whose birth is secondary information and indirect evidence (an age worked into a year), its residence primary, its parents a relationship FamilySearch computed; the birth register's own birth primary and direct, each record named by the original it was copied from

steps.say: the 1940 household page arrives through the inbox
the mother accepted: the mother-son link
the father accepted: the couple and the father-son link

expect.why: a census index's birth is a year worked from the father's age on the census day: a derivative, secondary information, indirect evidence, copied from the 1940 schedule
the census's own residence is the one thing it records first hand
the son's father and mother stand in FamilySearch's own Parents and Siblings table, computed from the household, not stated by the census
the record's fields say Birth though its heading says Death: the birth register's own birth, read from its index, is primary information and direct evidence
